title: Kodiak shift: annotated handoff & temporary runbook
content:
Purpose: quick, personal handoff for the Kodiak night shift. Mix of context, concise triage steps, and temporary fixes I used tonight. Not a replacement for canonical runbook — file as a scratch draft for later formalization.

Top-of-shift summary (what I observed):
- Rolling deploy of runtime v2.14 started ~21:05 UTC; ~21:18 deploy job retried for nodegroup A (OOM on gpu-03). Autoscaler spun new instance, but p95 latency spiked.
- After the retry, I saw intermittently corrupted tokenization in ~0.02% of requests for hosted-api model redwood-7b-v1 (examples attached below). Suspect KV cache/quantization path mismatch on warm-up.
- Alerts fired: latency-p95-hosted-api > 250ms for 10m, error-rate-chat > 1% for 5m.

Key signals / where to look first:
- Observability dashboards: Console > Routes > hosted-api / model=redwood-7b-v1 - check token-level timing breakdown (tokenize -> generate -> stream).
- Tracing: open trace sample for slow request, follow cache-hit/cold paths.
- Logs: serving-runtime logs on gpu-03 and gpu-07 for stacktraces relating to kvcache or incompatible kernels.
- Redis (prefix-cache): monitor hit_rate and eviction counters.

Immediate triage checklist (fastest possible actions):
1) Verify current deploy status (k8s): 
   - kubectl -n serving get pods -l release=runtime-v2.14 -o wide
   - kubectl -n serving logs <pod> -c runtime | tail -n 200 (start with pods on gpu-03)
2) Check Redis prefix/KV cache: 
   - redis-cli -h redis-main INFO stats | egrep "keyspace_hits|keyspace_misses|evicted_keys"
   - If miss rate >> hits and evicted_keys rising: consider temporary TTL increase or pause aggressive caching ops.
3) If token corruption observed, attempt cache bypass for a small percentage: 
   - Toggle route-level param: X-Cache-Bypass: true for 5% of requests (canary) via console quick patch.
   - If corruption stops for bypassed requests -> cache is culprit.
4) Rollback deploy to last known-stable (only if wider impact persists >30m): 
   - Initiate canary rollback in console: set active revision -> previous stable. Notify release-engineering.

Temporary remediation steps I applied (notes):
- Increased kv-cache TTL on redis namespace serving-prefix from 60s -> 180s (temporary) to reduce eviction churn; watch mem usage (dc metrics).
- For two pods on gpu-03 showing kernel-invalidation warnings I triggered a restart: kubectl -n serving rollout restart deployment/runtime-gpu-03-pool --timeout=5m. Post-restart p95 returned to ~210ms after 7 minutes.
- Enabled route fallback to cheaper variant (redwood-7b-v1-quantized) under routing policy for the affected region to reduce GPU pressure. That lowered tail latencies but introduced small regression in output style (noted in discipline: eval set #small-chat).

Escalation thresholds (what to call SRE/RE on):
- If p95 > 300ms for 15m AND error-rate > 1.5% -> pager to eng-serving-runtime oncall.
- If tokenization corruption > 0.1% of requests and reproduces on bypassed cache -> page research/rlhf team (possible model artifact).
- If redis eviction rate grows past 1k/min or memory > 75% for >5m -> page infra-db.

Reproduction notes (examples I captured):
- Bad output example: \"User: write a summary
 Response: \u0000...\u000bWhat do\" (NUL bytes + truncated tokens). Observed at 21:24 UTC on request id: req-20250108-2124-az3.
- Steps that increased chance of repro: bursty requests with long prefixes (>= 1024 tokens) while a pod was still warming KV cache after a restart.

Permanent fix ideas (to formalize into product tickets):
- Add cache versioning header tied to runtime kernel checksum; ignore cached entries if checksum mismatch.
- Improve warm-start for pods: pre-warm kv cache for top-n prefixes during rollout.
- Regression test: simple fuzz harness that verifies serialized token sequences don't contain unprintable characters after cache retrieval.

Commands & quick helpers (copy-paste):
- Check pod restarts: kubectl -n serving get pods -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,RESTARTS:.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- Grep logs for kernel warnings: kubectl -n serving logs <pod> -c runtime | egrep "kernel|kvcache|quantiz" -n
- Bypass cache for testing (example header): curl -H \"X-Cache-Bypass:true\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Notes for next shift (actionable tasks):
- Liam: follow up with infra-db about redis memory trend and whether we can bump instance class (ticket JIRA-OPS-7421).
- Priya: formalize the cache-versioning RFC; include kernel checksum approach and propose a rollout plan.
- I will attach the three sample request ids (req-20250108-2124-az3, req-20250108-2131-bt9, req-20250108-2139-qm2) to the confluence notes and add the raw payloads.

Open questions / TODOs (for triage doc):
- Is there a safe, fast way to invalidate only 'hot' prefixes during a bad rollout without full cache flush?
- How did the deploy choose gpu-03 for the first wave? (scheduling affinity or binpacking?) Link to release job: github PR above.

Raw debugging timeline (concise):
- 21:05 deploy started (v2.14)
- 21:18 first OOM on gpu-03 pod; pod restarted, autoscaler spawned new node.
- 21:20 latency p95 spikes to 380ms; alerts fire at 21:22.
- 21:24 observed corrupted tokens for first time: req-20250108-2124-az3.
- 21:30 increased redis TTL, restarted offending pods.
- 21:37 enabled quantized fallback for affected route.

Closing note: I left the temporary TTL bump and quantized fallback in place — both reduced visible impact but are stopgaps. Please do not make these permanent changes without cross-team sign-off. I added comments on the confluence page and linked evidence. Ping me (Maya) in slack @maya.chen if you need handover voice call — I will be available for the first 30 minutes after shift end.

End of notes.

Appendix: quick list of artifacts to attach (when moving to final runbook):
- log snippets (gpu-03, gpu-07)
- sample corrupted request payloads (3 ids)
- timeline + grafana screenshots of redis/memory/latency
- PRs: serving-runtime PR 412, rollout job logs
